_note: Machine-readable copy of the owner's decision queue. `context/pending_approval.md` is the prose record Simon writes each sweep; this file is the same decisions as rows, so a dashboard can show them without anyone reading the paragraphs. PressFlow reads this file from main (raw.githubusercontent) and falls back to editorial-factory/context/approvals.json when it cannot. Keep item order: open decisions first, then approved/in build, then closed.

items.headline: Mark our own test visits so traffic numbers mean something
items.detail: Done 2026-10-19 (`18ff5f1`): one classifier marks our own suites, probes and browsers as internal, so visitor numbers now mean real people. Browser suites send the header, the metered agent route marks itself, and any of our browsers can be marked by visiting once with ?factory_internal=1. The growth check reports the visitor/internal/unclassified split and gates on visitors only; earlier rows stay unclassified rather than being re-labelled. Remaining: the traffic_class column migration (0004) waits on your Supabase SQL editor — the marker works without it, from the payload.
items.impact: Visitors are now countable; every traffic gate is scored on real people.

items.headline: One copy of the W-2 vs 1099 and RSU hold-vs-sell engines — giniloh.com
items.detail: The factory-repo duplicate (src/lib/calc/*.ts + 11 vitest) and the two scripts that copied code into /root/giniloh are deleted. The live giniloh.com copy is the single home, and scripts/check-calculators.mjs now pins ~50 known answers from the 2026 spec vector, so a changed constant fails instead of quietly changing someone's pay numbers.
items.impact: Closed 2026-10-19: one engine per calculator, drift impossible, regressions caught locally.

items.headline: One-line fix for the IDE header gap and gutter alignment
items.detail: Done 2026-10-19: the owner's `@Simon fix the header gap` was applied to the shared chrome. Three defects, all measured on the rendered DOM rather than argued from a screenshot: (1) `IdeTextarea`'s header still relied on `justify-between` alone, so at 375 px its badge box overran the bar and painted over the file title (measured −34.0 px on spendproof/caseproof/parcelproof/facturgate); both chrome bars now carry `gap-x-3` + `flex-wrap`, `min-w-0`/`truncate` on the title, `shrink-0` on the badge group, and print only the claim ("ZERO EGRESS") below `sm` with the full label returning at ≥640 px. (2) the Recovery-summary badge on /parcelproof was being squeezed into a two-line pill ("3"/"flags") by the description beside it — `shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap` + `min-w-0` on the text block. (3) `tests/e2e/text-geometry.spec.ts` now measures the chrome BOXES (not glyph runs, and not skipping a clipped title) at 1280 px and 375 px on all four products; proven to bite by reverting the components (−34.0 px, 4 failed) and green with the fix. Gate: tsc, eslint 0 errors, 397/397 unit, build, 96/96 Playwright, visual-QA 24/24. Live: apps.aichieve.net/parcelproof and /caseproof measured after deploy.
items.impact: Closed — the chrome badge never touches the file title at 1280 px or 375 px, and a build-time geometry guard keeps it that way.

items.headline: Supplier geolocation pre-flight audit for the EU deforestation rules (EUDR)
items.detail: A model reads the declared fields out of supplier packs; overlap, declared-vs-computed area and scope are checked by our own geometry. Plan in five slices, S1 engine through S5 gate + deploy.
items.impact: Build in progress since 2026-10-18. EUDR application date is 30 December 2026.

items.headline: A power-bill audit that shows what one peak costs for a year
items.detail: Approved 2026-10-19 by the owner's `@Simon approve RatchetProof` (the only open row at the gate). Build dispatched as a one-shot job; v1 scope in `.hermes/plans/2026-10-19_ratchetproof-build.md`: deterministic core (coincident-interval align, billing window, billed demand = max(month peak, ratchet% × trailing-lookback peak, contract min), carry-over ledger), tariff/bill extraction in front of it (every field `extracted|unreadable|unstated`; an unreadable clause blocks the month), `/ratchetproof` UI, WebMCP `audit_demand_billing` at $1.50/call, web tier $12 one-off / $39/mo per site, registry `beta`.
items.impact: In build — a commercial power-bill audit that names the half hour which set the account's demand floor and prices it for the year. Launch call (beta → live) stays with the owner.

items.headline: aichieve.net has no robots.txt and no sitemap.xml
items.detail: Done 2026-10-19, verified live: https://aichieve.net/robots.txt answers 200 (66 B — `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `Sitemap: https://aichieve.net/sitemap.xml`) and https://aichieve.net/sitemap.xml answers 200 as a sitemap index pointing at sitemap-0.xml, which lists 110 URLs (home, article paths, hubs, /about/) — three listed paths re-probed 200. Closed on the owner's instruction `@Simon aichieve robots and sitemap`; no code change was needed from the factory because the front already serves both.
items.impact: Closed — crawlers and AI agents get a rule set and a sitemap to follow on aichieve.net.

items.headline: Delete the last QuarterLine references
items.detail: Done 2026-10-19: the legacy plugin descriptor was DELETED (it advertised the killed product and an /openapi.json URL that answered 404, so there was nothing correct to rewrite it to). The one agent descriptor that remains is /.well-known/mcp.json, which is generated from the live inventory. A guard test now fails the build when any /.well-known file names a retired product, slug or tool, and the receipt sender no longer names the retired product either.
items.impact: Closed — no published descriptor or customer email names a product we no longer sell.
